name: Spatial Configuration as Determinant of Social Encounter Frequency and Quality
short_description: Spatial integration determines encounter frequency; context determines encounter valence; visual connectivity determines social monitoring load; edges enable social choice
structural_pattern: Spatial configuration creates conditions for social encounter by determining WHO encounters WHOM, HOW OFTEN, and in WHAT CONTEXT. Space Syntax integration predicts co-presence: high-integration spaces are where paths converge, making encounter likely. Social encounters are PE events: encountering another person means encountering an agent whose behavior must be predicted. EXPECTED encounters in high-integration social spaces → low social PE → pleasant, bonding. UNEXPECTED encounters in low-integration spaces → high social PE → T5 threat assessment → anxiety. Visual connectivity (who can see whom) affects social monitoring and perceived privacy. Edge conditions (boundaries between public paths and semi-private zones) create OPTIONAL social encounter: places where a person can choose to engage or withdraw.
higher_order_principle: The social dimension of spatial prediction. As SC1 describes how configuration determines NAVIGATIONAL prediction, SC4 describes how it determines SOCIAL prediction: probability, context, and valence of encountering other people. Open-plan offices are the canonical negative case: high visual co-presence + no edges → chronic elevated social PE → attention fatigue, paradoxically reduced meaningful interaction.

encounter_valence_conditions.expected_social_space: High-integration social space (break room, lobby) → low social PE → positive valence
encounter_valence_conditions.unexpected_isolated_space: Low-integration space (dead-end, parking garage) → high social PE → T5 threat → anxiety

open_plan_problem.high_visual_connectivity: Constant social monitoring → social brain always active
open_plan_problem.result: Chronic elevated social PE → distraction, reduced deep work, withdrawal into headphones/screens

causal_links.evidence_base: One of the best-validated Space Syntax findings: integration predicts pedestrian density, which predicts encounter frequency. (Hillier, 1996)
Expected encounters in social spaces → positive. Unexpected encounters in non-social spaces → T5 threat. (Gehl, 1971/2011)
Open-plan environments maintain social brain in continuous monitoring mode. Cumulative social PE load → T25 attentional fatigue. (Kim & de Dear, 2013)
Edges (alcoves, window seats, setbacks) allow occupants to CHOOSE engagement or withdrawal. Optional activities increase with edge quality. (Gehl, 2010)

scope_conditions: Applies to all multi-occupant buildings and urban spaces
Effect strongest in buildings where social interaction is primary function (offices, schools, hospitals)
Cultural norms modulate social encounter preferences
Digital communication reduces dependency on spatial co-presence but embodied encounter remains psychologically distinct
moderators: Occupant density: spatial configuration creates CONDITIONS; density determines whether encounters occur
Cultural norms: social distance preferences, greeting rituals, eye-contact norms
Organizational hierarchy: encounters between status levels may carry higher social PE
Time of day: social expectations differ (corridor at 2pm vs. 2am)
Control: voluntary social spaces (café) vs. forced social spaces (open-plan desk)

interactions.nature: SC1 determines WHERE people move; SC4 determines WHERE people MEET. Integration predicts both.
Unexpected social encounters in low-integration spaces activate T5 threat assessment.
Chronic social monitoring in high-visibility environments taxes directed attention → T25 fatigue.
SC2 isovist area determines visual access between occupants → visual component of social monitoring load.
